a5555.t:
SHINYANGA: THE government has reassured the public that the Fire and Rescue Force is working tirelessly around the clock to rescue all mine workers trapped in the Nyandolwa Gold Mine in Shinyanga.
As of Saturday, five workers had been rescued: Three found alive, one who passed away while receiving treatment at the hospital and another found dead inside the mine.
Rescue operations are ongoing to locate the remaining 20 miners still trapped underground.
Deputy Minister for Home Affairs, Mr Daniel Sillo visited the site over the weekend and reaffirmed the commitment of rescue teams to continue their efforts without pause.
He insisted the critical importance of strict adherence to safety procedures in mining operations and urged mine owners across the country to prioritise safe working conditions to prevent such tragedies.
The accident occurred last Monday at a site licensed to a small-scale miners’ group called Wachapakazi.
At the time, approximately 25 workers were conducting maintenance at several gold mining pits.
Shinyanga District Commissioner Julius Mtatiro, who also provided an update on the rescue mission, vowed to persist until all missing workers are found and brought to safety.
“We must keep fighting until everyone is out safely. President Samia Suluhu Hassan has issued special directives which are being actively implemented, including reinforcements from the Prime Minister’s Office and the Fire and Rescue Force,” Mtatiro stated.
President Samia Suluhu Hassan has instructed the Prime Minister’s Office to collaborate closely with defence and security agencies to accelerate rescue operations and ordered immediate humanitarian assistance for the victims. In a message posted on her social media last Thursday, President Samia expressed deep sorrow over the tragedy.
“I have received with great sadness reports of the disaster at Nyandolwa Mine, where 25 of our fellow citizens were trapped by debris. Let us continue praying for the quick recovery of the injured and may the bereaved families find strength and comfort during this difficult time,” she wrote.
ALSO READ: Chile mine collapse: Search ends after 5 miners found dead
Regional authorities confirmed that four miners had been rescued, although 27-year-old Emanuel Kija later succumbed to injuries sustained during the incident.
Deputy Minister for Minerals Stephen Kiruswa, who visited the site on Wednesday, confirmed Kija’s death.
“We are working around the clock. Communication with the trapped miners has been established and they are still alive as of now. I have instructed that all necessary first aid supplies, including oxygen machines, be brought to the site immediately,” Mr Kiruswa said.
Preliminary investigations suggest that the mining shafts were constructed too close to each other, requiring frequent repairs to prevent erosion and collapse.
The deputy minister has tasked mining experts and the Mining Commission with assessing the site’s safety and recommending measures for safer mining operations.
Mr Mtatiro detailed that Shaft No 130 had six workers when the collapse occurred; four were rescued (including the late Kija). Shaft No 20 had eight miners and the remainder were in Shaft No 103.
“We are in constant contact with rescue teams and progress is being made. We urge residents to remain calm as operations continue at full force,” Mtatiro added.
The three confirmed survivors are Furano Peter, Antony Clement and Nagula Japhet. One of the mine owners, Fikiri Mnwagi, explained that the collapse happened during rehabilitation works on the shafts, triggered by underground tremors that destabilised the ground, causing the soil to collapse from the base upwards.

a5627.t:
Budget 2025 du Niger : 3 033 milliards de CFA et des réformes fiscales pour stimuler l’économie
Le gouvernement nigérien a adopté mardi le projet d’ordonnance portant loi de finances pour l’année budgétaire 2025. Équilibré en ressources et en charges à 3 033,33 milliards de francs CFA, le budget enregistre une hausse de 4,13 % par rapport à 2024.
Le texte, approuvé en Conseil des ministres du 31 décembre 2024, introduit une série de nouvelles mesures fiscales destinées à relancer l’économie et à renforcer les recettes publiques. Parmi celles-ci figurent l’institution d’un impôt sur les plus-values de cessions des titres miniers, une révision de la liste des exonérations de l’impôt sur les bénéfices (ISB) et une augmentation du taux de cet impôt pour les non-résidents. La TVA sera désormais appliquée aux ventes en ligne, et une nouvelle taxe sur les admissions temporaires, y compris leurs prorogations et mutations, sera instaurée.
En parallèle, les bons de commandes publics seront soumis à une obligation d’enregistrement et un droit de timbre minimum sera appliqué sur les documents fiscaux, notamment les attestations d’exonération fiscale périodique et les attestations de dispense de retenue à la source de la TVA. Le régime fiscal synthétique perdra l’exonération de deux ans accordée aux nouvelles entreprises.
Ce projet de loi exempte, par ailleurs, la profession de journaliste du régime d’imposition et facilite le paiement de la taxe professionnelle pour les établissements privés d’enseignement. Il exonère aussi les véhicules neufs destinés au transport des marchandises ou des voyageurs de droits et taxes à l’importation, à l’exception de la redevance statistique et des prélèvements communautaires.
Le projet prévoit aussi la soumission des ONG, projets et association de développement au droit de communication, ainsi que l’application de la redevance statistique à l’exportation sur les produits agro- sylvo-pastoraux.
À noter que les dépenses de l’État pour 2025 sont fixées à 2 526,72 milliards de francs CFA, avec des charges de trésorerie estimées à 506,61 milliards. Ces dépenses couvrent notamment les pécules des contractuels, des investissements prioritaires, ainsi que des dépenses sociales dans les secteurs de la santé et de l’éducation.
Ce projet de loi, élaboré dans le cadre des orientations budgétaires 2025-2027, ambitionne de relancer l’économie et accroître le pouvoir d’achat des populations dans un contexte marqué par des crises internationales, mais surtout par les effets des sanctions économiques et financières subies par le pays suite au coup d’État militaire du 26 juillet 2023.
a5627.en:
Niger's 2025 Budget: 3,033 billion CFA francs and tax reforms to stimulate the economy

The Nigerien government adopted on Tuesday the draft ordinance constituting the finance law for the 2025 budget year. Balanced in resources and expenditures at 3,033.33 billion CFA francs, the budget records an increase of 4.13% compared with 2024.

The text, approved in the Council of Ministers of 31 December 2024, introduces a series of new tax measures intended to revive the economy and strengthen public revenues. Among these are the institution of a tax on capital gains from the transfer of mining titles, a revision of the list of exemptions from the tax on profits (ISB) and an increase in the rate of that tax for non-residents. VAT will henceforth be applied to online sales, and a new tax on temporary admissions, including their extensions and transfers, will be introduced.

In parallel, public purchase orders will be subject to a registration requirement and a minimum stamp duty will be applied to tax documents, in particular periodic tax-exemption certificates and certificates of exemption from VAT withholding at source. The simplified tax regime will lose the two-year exemption granted to new businesses.

This bill also exempts the profession of journalist from the taxation regime and facilitates payment of the business tax for private teaching establishments. It also exempts new vehicles intended for the transport of goods or passengers from import duties and taxes, with the exception of the statistical levy and community levies.

The draft also provides for subjecting NGOs, projects and development associations to the duty of disclosure, as well as the application of the statistical export levy to agro-silvo-pastoral products.

It should be noted that State expenditure for 2025 is set at 2,526.72 billion CFA francs, with treasury charges estimated at 506.61 billion. These expenditures cover in particular the stipends of contract staff, priority investments, as well as social spending in the health and education sectors.

This bill, drawn up within the framework of the 2025-2027 budget orientations, aims to revive the economy and increase the purchasing power of the population in a context marked by international crises, but above all by the effects of the economic and financial sanctions suffered by the country following the military coup d'état of 26 July 2023.

a5790.t: O Millennium Challenge Corporation, MCC, aprovou, ontem, um financiamento de 500 milhões de dólares norte-americanos para a implementação do Compacto-II em Moçambique. Segundo um comunicado enviado à nossa redacção, a assinatura do Acordo de Financiamento entre os Governos de Moçambique e dos Estados Unidos, através do MCC, está prevista para Setembro deste ano, em Washington DC. O compacto-II, aprovado em Washington, nos Estados Unidos da América, terá como enfoque a província da Zambézia, cobrindo três áreas: Promoção de Investimento na Agricultura Comercial; Conectividade e Transporte Rural, Mudanças Climáticas e Desenvolvimento Costeiro.
a5790.en: The Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) yesterday approved US$500 million in financing for the implementation of Compact II in Mozambique. According to a statement sent to our newsroom, the signing of the Financing Agreement between the Governments of Mozambique and the United States, through the MCC, is scheduled for September this year in Washington DC. Compact II, approved in Washington in the United States of America, will focus on Zambézia province, covering three areas: Promotion of Investment in Commercial Agriculture; Rural Connectivity and Transport; and Climate Change and Coastal Development.

a5835.t:
THE Chas Everitt International Property Group says it is looking to expand its footprint into several new countries across the continent.
This follows the leading real estate firm’s expansion into Zimbabwe to make inroads into the growing luxury property market that is attracting affluent buyers and investors.
Speaking at the grand opening of the group’s office in Zimbabwe, Chas Everitt COO Barry Davies said that despite some challenges, including currency instability and regulatory uncertainties, the group believes that Zimbabwe’s residential real estate sector holds tremendous potential for growth.
“We are highly cognisant of the fundamental role that the real estate and housing sector plays in driving economic development, and we strongly believe that our entry is more than just a business expansion; it is a vote of confidence in Zimbabwe’s future,” Davies said in the capital this week.
He said Zimbabwe’s residential real estate sector is expected to be worth over US$85 billion this year and grow at an annual rate exceeding five percent.
“Our decision to expand into Zimbabwe is a testament to the country’s steady economic recovery and its rapid growth in key industries such as mining, tourism, and agriculture,” he said.
“The surge in diaspora spending, coupled with government policy reforms and infrastructure developments, has created a thriving property market that is attracting affluent buyers and investors from around the world.”
He added that the group will cater to the growing demand for prime residential properties in suburbs such as Avondale, Borrowdale, and Mount Pleasant.
Chas Everitt will provide real estate services including sales, leasing and property management in the country.
Over the last two decades, Chas Everitt has spread its reach to 72 countries, 550 companies, and 4800 offices.
Speaking at the event, permanent secretary for Legal Affairs, Vimbai Nyemba, said Zimbabwe strives to create an enabling environment that attracts investors.
“Our ministry plays an instrumental role in shaping Zimbabwe’s economic trajectory by ensuring that our legal frameworks are conducive to investment while also safeguarding national interests,” Nyemba said.
She highlighted that legal certainty, contract enforcement and protection of property rights are critical factors in maintaining investor confidence.
“We are steadfast in our commitment to strengthening Zimbabwe’s legal environment and upholding the rule of law there by creating a stable and predictable business climate,” she said.
Nyemba commended Chas Everitt for establishing its footprint in Zimbabwe, highlighting that it is a clear testament of the confidence that international investors have in the country’s resilience, potential and unwavering commitment to economic transformation.

a5844.t:
« L’ONU a été créée par le monde, pour le monde». Ce sont les mots du Secrétaire Général de l’organisation mondiale, dans son message à l’occasion de la célébration du 79e anniversaire de l’Organisation des Nations unies. Un anniversaire quelque peu entaché par la tragédie humaine qui se déroule actuellement à Gaza et même au Liban. Les appels mettre fin à la furie génocidaire de l’entité sioniste restent lettre morte, pendant que les populations civiles subissent des souffrances indicibles.
Si la situation en Palestine occupée expose, dans sa brutalité crue, les failles structurelles d’une organisation piégée dans ses propres mécanismes et paralysée par le cynisme de quelques puissances, elle ne doit pas masquer les efforts déployés par l’ONU en matière de coopération internationale afin de faire face aux multiples défis de la planète. Cette volonté d’unir les forces mondiales résonne particulièrement à Djibouti, dont la position géostratégique en fait un acteur clé sur la scène internationale, notamment en tant que plaque tournante pour l’aide humanitaire.
L’engagement de l’ONU à Djibouti se manifeste tant sur le plan humanitaire que sur le développement durable. Face à la sécheresse qui frappe la région depuis 2022, plus de 4 millions de dollars ont été mobilisés pour assurer la sécurité alimentaire de 90 000 personnes et améliorer l’accès à l’eau pour 140 000 habitants. Ces efforts sont essentiels pour un pays comme le nôtre, qui subit les effets du changement climatique tout en étant une terre d’accueil pour des réfugiés et des migrants en quête de sécurité.
Dans cette optique, l’inauguration de nouveaux bureaux de l’Organisation internationale pour les Migrations (OIM) dans la région de Dikhil marque la volonté de l’ONU d’étendre sa présence dans tout le territoire djiboutien. Cette extension renforce la proximité entre l’organisation et les populations locales, permettant ainsi de mieux répondre aux besoins des réfugiés, des demandeurs d’asile et des migrants.
Des avancées notables ont été réalisées dans des domaines cruciaux comme l’éducation, la santé et l’égalité des genres. La République de Djibouti se distingue comme pionnière en matière de droits des réfugiés à l’éducation, offrant un accès à l’enseignement secondaire à des milliers d’enfants réfugiés. Cette garantie pour l’éducation s’inscrit dans une démarche plus large de l’ONU pour promouvoir le développement humain durable.
De plus, la lutte contre la malnutrition, à travers la mise en œuvre d’un Plan national multisectoriel de nutrition, témoigne d’une coopération efficace entre les agences du système onusien et le gouvernement djiboutien dans le secteur de la santé. Ce type de collaboration est essentiel pour améliorer les conditions de vie des populations locales.
Les initiatives concernant l’égalité des genres, notamment l’ODD 5, sont également à saluer. La création du premier « One Stop Center » à Djibouti pour lutter contre les violences basées sur le genre représente un pas en avant significatif vers une société plus égalitaire et plus juste.
En tant que hub logistique de l’ONU, le pays joue un rôle vital dans l’acheminement de l’aide humanitaire vers des régions en crise, notamment la Corne de l’Afrique et le Yémen. Cette dimension régionale renforce l’importance de Djibouti sur la scène internationale et fait du pays un pilier de la stabilité dans une région en proie à des tensions multiples. Pour Djibouti, ce partenariat avec l’ONU est un atout majeur pour affronter les défis présents et à venir, tant sur le plan national que régional.
a5844.en:
"The UN was created by the world, for the world." These are the words of the Secretary-General of the world organization, in his message on the occasion of the celebration of the 79th anniversary of the United Nations Organization. An anniversary somewhat tarnished by the human tragedy currently unfolding in Gaza and even in Lebanon. The calls to put an end to the genocidal fury of the Zionist entity remain a dead letter, while civilian populations endure unspeakable suffering.

If the situation in occupied Palestine exposes, in its raw brutality, the structural flaws of an organization trapped in its own mechanisms and paralyzed by the cynicism of a few powers, it must not mask the efforts deployed by the UN in the area of international cooperation in order to face the planet's multiple challenges. This will to unite global forces resonates particularly in Djibouti, whose geostrategic position makes it a key actor on the international stage, notably as a hub for humanitarian aid.

The UN's engagement in Djibouti is manifest on both the humanitarian and the sustainable development fronts. Faced with the drought that has struck the region since 2022, more than 4 million dollars have been mobilized to ensure food security for 90,000 people and to improve access to water for 140,000 inhabitants. These efforts are essential for a country like ours, which suffers the effects of climate change while being a land of welcome for refugees and migrants in search of safety.

In this perspective, the inauguration of new offices of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in the Dikhil region marks the UN's will to extend its presence throughout Djiboutian territory. This extension strengthens the proximity between the organization and local populations, thus making it possible to respond better to the needs of refugees, asylum seekers and migrants.

Notable advances have been achieved in crucial areas such as education, health and gender equality. The Republic of Djibouti stands out as a pioneer in the matter of refugees' rights to education, offering access to secondary education to thousands of refugee children. This guarantee for education is part of a broader UN approach to promoting sustainable human development.

In addition, the fight against malnutrition, through the implementation of a multisectoral National Nutrition Plan, bears witness to effective cooperation between the agencies of the UN system and the Djiboutian government in the health sector. This type of collaboration is essential to improving the living conditions of local populations.

The initiatives concerning gender equality, notably SDG 5, are also to be saluted. The creation of the first "One Stop Center" in Djibouti to combat gender-based violence represents a significant step forward toward a more egalitarian and more just society.

As a logistics hub for the UN, the country plays a vital role in the delivery of humanitarian aid to regions in crisis, notably the Horn of Africa and Yemen. This regional dimension reinforces Djibouti's importance on the international stage and makes the country a pillar of stability in a region prey to multiple tensions. For Djibouti, this partnership with the UN is a major asset for confronting present and future challenges, both nationally and regionally.

a6168.t:
L’Afrique possède plus de 165 milliards de dollars de capitaux nationaux inexploités qui pourraient stimuler le développement du continent et réduire sa dépendance aux financements extérieurs volatiles, ont révélé jeudi des experts financiers lors des Assemblées annuelles de la Banque africaine de développement.
Lors d’une table ronde de haut niveau intitulée « Tirer le meilleur parti du capital de l’Afrique », Abena Amoah, directrice générale de la Bourse du Ghana, a livré des chiffres saisissants. « Rien qu’en Afrique de l’Ouest, entre le Ghana et le Nigéria, nous avons des fonds de pension qui représentent près de 40 milliards de dollars et qui placent plus de 90 % de leurs actifs sous gestion dans des titres d’État, sous prétexte qu’ils n’ont pas d’opportunités d’investissement », a-t-elle indiqué.
La dirigeante a également souligné un paradoxe frappant. A l’en croire, en 2024, les Africains ont investi 125 milliards de dollars dans les cryptomonnaies, le Nigéria contribuant à lui seul pour 65 milliards, devenant ainsi la deuxième base mondiale d’investisseurs crypto après l’Inde.
Denys Denya, vice-président exécutif d’Afreximbank, a présenté des résultats encourageants avec le Programme de dépôt des banques centrales, qui a fait passer les dépôts institutionnels africains de 14 millions de dollars en 2014 à plus de 34 milliards aujourd’hui.
L’institution a également diversifié ses sources de financement vers les marchés japonais et chinois pour réduire sa dépendance aux marchés occidentaux.
Les panélistes ont identifié plusieurs freins majeurs : l’instabilité macroéconomique, des taux d’intérêt dépassant 20 % sur certains marchés, et des goulets d’étranglement réglementaires pénalisant particulièrement les femmes et jeunes entrepreneurs.
Solomon Quaynor, vice-président de la BAD, a pointé un enjeu critique. « Nous parlons de 2 100 milliards de dollars d’actifs sous gestion provenant des fonds de pension, des compagnies d’assurance et des fonds souverains africains. Mais plus de 80 % de cette somme est immobilisée dans les trésoreries publiques », a-t-il relevé.
Selon S&P Global, l’Afrique devrait atteindre une croissance de 4,8 % en 2025, nettement supérieure à la moyenne mondiale de 3 %. L’agence de notation a procédé à 11 ajustements positifs des notes souveraines africaines l’année précédente.
La table ronde a appelé à un changement de paradigme : abandonner la dépendance excessive à l’aide étrangère au profit de stratégies d’investissement audacieuses menées par les pays africains eux-mêmes, avec le développement urgent de marchés de capitaux sophistiqués pour canaliser ces ressources vers des investissements productifs.
ARD/ac/Sf/APA
a6168.en:
Africa possesses more than 165 billion dollars of untapped domestic capital that could boost the continent's development and reduce its dependence on volatile external financing, financial experts revealed on Thursday at the Annual Meetings of the African Development Bank.

During a high-level round table entitled "Making the most of Africa's capital", Abena Amoah, Director General of the Ghana Stock Exchange, delivered striking figures. "In West Africa alone, between Ghana and Nigeria, we have pension funds that represent close to 40 billion dollars and that place more than 90% of their assets under management in government securities, on the pretext that they have no investment opportunities," she said.

The executive also highlighted a striking paradox. According to her, in 2024 Africans invested 125 billion dollars in cryptocurrencies, with Nigeria alone contributing 65 billion, thus becoming the world's second-largest base of crypto investors after India.

Denys Denya, Executive Vice-President of Afreximbank, presented encouraging results with the Central Bank Deposit Programme, which has raised African institutional deposits from 14 million dollars in 2014 to more than 34 billion today.

The institution has also diversified its funding sources towards the Japanese and Chinese markets in order to reduce its dependence on Western markets.

The panellists identified several major obstacles: macroeconomic instability, interest rates exceeding 20% in some markets, and regulatory bottlenecks that particularly penalise women and young entrepreneurs.

Solomon Quaynor, Vice-President of the AfDB, pointed to a critical issue. "We are talking about 2,100 billion dollars of assets under management coming from African pension funds, insurance companies and sovereign wealth funds. But more than 80% of that sum is locked up in public treasuries," he noted.

According to S&P Global, Africa should reach growth of 4.8% in 2025, well above the global average of 3%. The rating agency made 11 positive adjustments to African sovereign ratings in the previous year.

The round table called for a paradigm shift: abandoning excessive dependence on foreign aid in favour of bold investment strategies led by African countries themselves, with the urgent development of sophisticated capital markets to channel these resources towards productive investments.

ARD/ac/Sf/APA

a6239.t:
La Brigade mobile des douanes de Banfora de la région douanière de l’Ouest et le bureau des douanes de Léo de la région douanière du Centre-Sud ont, dans leur mission de lutte contre la fraude et de surveillance du territoire, procédé à des saisies de noix et d’amandes de karité conformément au communiqué conjoint des ministères en charge du Commerce et de l’Économie portant suspension temporaire de l’exportation d’amande de karité.
A Banfora, dans la région douanière de l’Ouest, il s’est agi de la saisie sur renseignement, de trois (03) camions chargés de noix de karité destinées à la Côte d’Ivoire sans aucune formalité (exportation en contrebande de marchandises soumises à Autorisation Spéciale). Cette opération qui s’est déroulée du 8 au 10 décembre 2024 a permis de saisir 𝐚𝐮 𝐭𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝟖𝟏 𝟐𝟖𝟎 𝐤𝐠 𝐝’𝐮𝐧𝐞 𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐮𝐫 𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐝𝐞 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐞 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐬𝐢𝐱 𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐞 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐞 (𝟒𝟎 𝟔𝟒𝟎 𝟎𝟎𝟎) 𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐬 𝐂𝐅𝐀.
A Léo, dans la région douanière du Centre-Sud, le Bureau des douanes a saisi une camionnette chargée de 150 sacs d’amandes de karité 𝐝’𝐮𝐧𝐞 𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐮𝐫 𝐭𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐞́𝐞 𝐚̀ 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐭𝐫𝐞 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐝𝐞𝐮𝐱 𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐞 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐞 (𝟒.𝟐𝟓𝟎.𝟎𝟎𝟎) 𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐬 𝐂𝐅𝐀, 𝐥𝐞 𝟒 𝐧𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐫𝐞 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟒.
Il faut noter que ces saisies ont été effectuées conformément au communiqué conjoint N°024012/MICA/MEF du 18 septembre 2024 portant suspension temporaire de l’exportation de l’amande de karité.
Tout en félicitant et encourageant les agents des offices des douanes concernés, le Directeur général des douanes, l’Inspecteur divisionnaire des douanes Adama ILBOUDO rappelle à tous les exportateurs d’amandes et de noix de karité que cette suspension a pour objectif de rendre disponibles ces matières premières pour nos unités industrielles de transformation au niveau national. Toute chose qui permet de s’aligner à la dynamique du Gouvernement visant à soutenir le développement de nos industries nationales.
Le Directeur général des douanes saisit cette opportunité pour interpeller tous les exportateurs d’amandes et de noix de karité au respect du communiqué conjoint de la suspension suscité et compte sur la vigilance des honnêtes citoyens afin d’éviter ces fraudes.
𝐋𝐚 𝐃𝐨𝐮𝐚𝐧𝐞 : 𝐇𝐨𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐮𝐫-𝐃𝐞́𝐯𝐨𝐮𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭-𝐕𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞
𝐒𝐂𝐑𝐏/𝐃𝐆𝐃
a6239.en:
The Banfora mobile customs brigade of the Western customs region and the Léo customs office of the Centre-South customs region, in their mission of combating fraud and territorial surveillance, carried out seizures of shea nuts and shea almonds in accordance with the joint communiqué of the ministries in charge of Trade and the Economy on the temporary suspension of shea almond exports.

In Banfora, in the Western customs region, this involved the seizure, on the basis of intelligence, of three (03) trucks loaded with shea nuts bound for Côte d'Ivoire without any formalities (smuggling of goods subject to Special Authorisation). This operation, which took place from 8 to 10 December 2024, made it possible to seize a total of 81,280 kg with an estimated value of forty million six hundred and forty thousand (40,640,000) CFA francs.

In Léo, in the Centre-South customs region, the customs office seized a van loaded with 150 bags of shea almonds with a total estimated value of four million two hundred and fifty thousand (4,250,000) CFA francs, on 4 November 2024.

It should be noted that these seizures were carried out in accordance with joint communiqué No. 024012/MICA/MEF of 18 September 2024 on the temporary suspension of shea almond exports.

While congratulating and encouraging the officers of the customs offices concerned, the Director General of Customs, Divisional Inspector of Customs Adama ILBOUDO, reminds all exporters of shea almonds and nuts that the purpose of this suspension is to make these raw materials available to our national industrial processing units. All of which makes it possible to align with the Government's drive to support the development of our national industries.

The Director General of Customs takes this opportunity to call on all exporters of shea almonds and nuts to comply with the aforementioned joint communiqué on the suspension, and counts on the vigilance of honest citizens in order to prevent such fraud.

Customs: Honour – Dedication – Vigilance

SCRP/DGD

a6376.t:
The Chartered Institute of Supply Chain Management-Ghana (CISCM) has inducted 134 individuals into its fold as part of efforts to develop and grow the supply chain industry.
The inductees comprise 88 full members, 25 subject matter experts, 12 fellows and eight associates.
The fellows include the Chief Executive Officer of University of Ghana Medical Center (UGMC), Dr Kwame Anim-Boamah; the Director of Nursing, UGMC, Judith Naa-Klorkor Asiamah ; former Secretary General, Ghana Trade Union Congress (TUC), Dr Kofi Asamoah;Managing Director of Coca-Cola Ghana, Felix Gomis; former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Professional Studies, Professor Joshua Alabi ; Director of AI Energy Group, Nana Kofi Tufour Antwi, and others.
The subject matter experts include the Presidential Advisor and Special Aid to the President, Joyce Bawah Mogtari; former Chief of Defence Staff, General Thomas Oppong-Peprah; the Chief Executive of Volta River Authority(VRA),Edward Obeng Kenzo; the Deputy CE of VRA, Kenneth Arthur; Presidential Advisor for 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development, Augustus Obuadum Tanoh and others.
Some associates are Adzika Hannah ;Angmortey Joshua; Bruce Mwintiro Kalinyah ; Kwame Darko Safo, Prosper Nyamedor and Rukayatu Abass.
The Lead Executive of CISCM, Richard Asante-Amoah, led them to make their declarations and affirmations.
The 6th induction and Investiture ceremony was held on the theme :”Integrated Supply Chain Management:A catalyst for Development.
Prioritise
The Presidential Advisor and Special Aid to the President, Mrs Mogtari, stressed the need to prioritise quality control, integrated trade, and environmental protection in order to harness the full benefits of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and achieve sustainable economic growth.
She said while the country had made great strides in stabilising the economy and strengthening diplomatic relations , those gains risked being undermined if the country did not address structural inefficiencies in its supply chain and trade systems.
Collective efforts
Mrs Mogtari called for a collective action to preserve water bodies, soil and the ecosystem, emphasising that environmental pollution undermined every effort the country made to build sustainable trade networks.
She said ,”Environmental degradation, particularly from illegal mining activities, is a major threat to the country’s agricultural exports and overall health of the economy”.
“Our farms are producing crops, but the produce is often contaminated by pollutants, making them unfit for human consumption. That defeats the entire purpose of building an integrated supply chain,” she said.
She commended the introduction of carbon credits, saying they provided an incentive to reforest degraded areas and promote alternative livelihoods to illegal mining.
Strengthen
The Group Head Supply Chain of Jospong Group of Companies, Hannah Boohemaa Otu, urged African businesses to strengthen local markets and ensure that locally produced goods and services remained competitive despite tariffs and external pressures.
Referencing the recent 10 per cent tariff imposed by the United States on African exports, she said African countries must reduce dependency on foreign aid and take control of their economic destiny.
“We can create a thriving business environment, strengthen local economies, and support currency stabilisation by prioritising quality, innovation and efficiency,” she added.
Ms Otu also called for enhanced free cash flow generation among businesses, stressing that integrated supply chain minded professionals must leverage technology for seamless data sharing, transparency and traceability.
Efforts
The President of CISCM, Richard Obeng Okrah, revealed that the institute was pursuing the enactment of a legislative instrument that would bring together all professional bodies involved in various components of the supply chain into an apex council.
He announced that the institute’s special initiative for the year would focus on five critical sectors of the economy- security, health, agriculture, extractive industry, energy to ensure value addition and supply chain excellence.

a6461.t:
The Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA) has recognised healthcare providers and journalists, rewarding them for their contributions to advancing Universal Health Coverage (UHC) in the state.
At an award ceremony commemorating the 2024 Universal Health Coverage Day, LASHMA honoured stakeholders who have demonstrated commitment to promoting its ILERA EKO Social Health Insurance Scheme.
Awards were presented to healthcare providers, including St Nicholas Hospitals, Aruna Ogun Memorial Specialist Hospital, and Esso Hospital, for their excellence in clinical care, patient safety, and community health initiatives.
Journalists Angela Onwuzoo of Punch Newspaper, Titilayo Abereowo of Channels Television, and Adeolu Okunade of the Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria (FRCN) were recognised for their impactful reporting and advocacy on health awareness.
LASHMA also acknowledged the contributions of healthcare professionals, such as Osinachi Ubani from Oshodi Primary Health Centre, and Dorcas Nyanah, Ikorodu General Hospital, who received awards for leadership in quality improvement and healthcare quality champion.
Achieving UHC in Lagos
In her remarks, the Permanent Secretary of LASHMA, Emmanuella Zamba, emphasised the significance of collaboration in achieving UHC.
“Your innovative approaches, dedication, and tireless advocacy are the backbone of our achievements,” Ms Zamba said. “Today, we celebrate not just the milestones but the extraordinary individuals and organisations that made them possible.”
“Through ILERA EKO, we are bridging gaps in healthcare access for all Lagosians,” Ms Zamba said.
She highlighted the scheme’s milestones, including over one million enrollees and the establishment of the Eko Social Health Alliance (EKOSHA) for vulnerable populations.
Recently, LASHMA revealed that over 1.3 million residents have been enrolled in the Ilera-Eko insurance scheme, noting that since the enactment of the Lagos State Health Scheme Law in 2015, the state has significantly advanced toward its UHC goals.
More comments
Speaking at the event, Permanent Secretary, Health District VI, Lagos State, Abimbola Mabogunje, commended LASHMA for the event, which she noted underscores the importance of health insurance in achieving UHC.
“Access to affordable healthcare should not lead to out-of-pocket financial strain. Health insurance bridges this gap, and ILERA EKO is a testament to that,” Ms Mabogunje said.
She commended LASHMA for its proactive efforts in reducing out-of-pocket expenses through health insurance.
“Primary healthcare is pivotal, and LASHMA is setting the pace for universal health access in Lagos,” she said.
Also, the Senior Health Specialist with USAID-LHSS, Chidumga Ohazurike, applauded LASHMA’s progress and recognised the vital role of healthcare providers.
Ms Ohazurike praised LASHMA’s achievements, stating: “We’ve witnessed LASHMA grow significantly, with impactful results that inspire confidence in the future of health insurance in Lagos.”

a6678.t:
By Gift Chiponde
Lilongwe, December 11, Mana:President Dr Lazarus Chakwera has expressed his appreciation to local organizations and development partners for their unwavering support and dedication in ensuring food availability to Malawians during this period of food security crisis.
The President stressed the importance of seeking international support to address the humanitarian crisis the country is currently grappling with.
President Chakwera recognised significant contributions that Malawi has received from various development partners through the World Food Programme (WFP).
He said WFP will publicly disclose the details of how and where the aid has been distributed.
He pointed out that Malawi has received substantial financial support from governments around the world through the World Food Program (WFP), including 11.8 million dollars from Sweden and the Netherlands, 7 million dollars from the United States, 3.8 million dollars from the United Kingdom, 1.9 million dollars from Japan, 1.6 million dollars from France, 1.5 million dollars from South Korea, and 1.07 million dollars from Germany.
Additionally, Norway and Iceland contributed 950,000 dollars, Denmark provided 750,000 dollars, Ireland donated 556,000 dollars, Switzerland contributed 500,000 dollars, and the African Development Bank donated 1 million dollars.
The President specifically commended partners such as Good Neighbors Malawi, Nkhoma Synod, Emerging Donor March Fund, Save the Children, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), BHA, FAO, Mary’s Meals, USAID, JBJ Foundation, ISRAID, and Caritas partners for their steadfast support.
He urged the partners to continue their efforts in mobilising support for Malawi from across the globe to alleviate the lives of Malawians.

a6781.t:
Entre Nous: Destituée pour incapacité à régler la crise sécuritaire !
Dans la nuit du jeudi 9 au vendredi 10 octobre 2025, le Congrès de Pérou a destitué la Présidente de la République, Dina Boluarte, âgée de 63 ans, pour incapacité morale permanente à exercer ses fonctions.
Elle avait pris les commandes du pays en décembre 2022, après la destitution de Pedro Castillo, dont le mandat devrait  prendre fin en juillet 2026. La Présidente Dina Boluarte a échappé à sept reprises à la destitution grâce au soutien de ses anciens alliés qui ont fini par la lâcher. 
Il est reproché principalement à l’ex-Présidente de Pérou et son gouvernement « leur incapacité à régler la crise sécuritaire ». Dina Boluarte et son équipe étaient tenus « responsables de l’insécurité qui assaille le pays et qui a coûté la vie à plus de 5000 personnes en trois ans ».  
Selon le quotidien péruvien El Comercio cité par Courrier international, « Dina Boluarte laisse un pays moins sûr, plus fragmenté et plus méfiant envers ses institutions ». « C’est l’épilogue d’une gestion qui, depuis ses débuts,  s’est caractérisée par une absence de direction et une incapacité à faire face aux défis les plus urgents du pays », précise le quotidien. 
Cette destitution a été accueillie avec joie par des centaines de Péruviens. Le Président du Parlement, José Jéri, 38 ans, a prêté serment pour prendre la tête de l’Etat. « J’assume avec humilité la présidence de la République, par succession constitutionnelle, afin de mettre en place et diriger un gouvernement de transition », a souligné José Jéri qui dirigera le pays jusqu’au 26 juillet 2026 avec la lourde tâche d’organiser les élections générales en avril prochain. 
Quant à Dina Boluarte, le ministère public péruvien a demandé à la justice de lui interdire de quitter le pays pendant 18 à 36 mois, afin de finaliser les enquêtes la visant pour « des délits de blanchiments d’actifs au préjudice de l’Etat » ; « corruption et abus de pouvoir ».
 Selon le ministère public, « cette mesure vise à garantir la présence de Boluarte pendant le déroulement du processus pénal et une éventuelle fuite du territoire national». Avant sa déchéance de la fonction présidentielle, l’exprésidente avait été secouée par plusieurs scandales portant sur l’acquisition par ses soins de montres et de bijoux et pour s’être permise « une rhinoplastie pratiquée en secret en 2023 en violation de la loi ». 
Pays de l’Amérique du Sud, le Pérou traverse depuis quelques années « la pire période d’instabilité politique de son histoire moderne, avec sept présidents en près de neuf ans ». 
Par Chiaka Doumbia
a6781.en:
Entre Nous: Removed from office for failing to resolve the security crisis!

On the night of Thursday 9 to Friday 10 October 2025, the Congress of Peru removed the President of the Republic, Dina Boluarte, aged 63, from office for permanent moral incapacity to exercise her functions.

She had taken the reins of the country in December 2022, after the removal of Pedro Castillo, whose term was to end in July 2026. President Dina Boluarte had escaped removal on seven occasions thanks to the support of her former allies, who ended up dropping her.

The main reproach against the former President of Peru and her government is "their inability to resolve the security crisis". Dina Boluarte and her team were held "responsible for the insecurity besetting the country, which has cost the lives of more than 5,000 people in three years".

According to the Peruvian daily El Comercio, cited by Courrier international, "Dina Boluarte leaves behind a country that is less safe, more fragmented and more distrustful of its institutions". "This is the epilogue of an administration that, from its very beginnings, was characterised by an absence of direction and an inability to confront the country's most urgent challenges," the newspaper specifies.

This removal was greeted with joy by hundreds of Peruvians. The President of Parliament, José Jéri, 38, was sworn in to take the helm of the State. "I assume the presidency of the Republic with humility, by constitutional succession, in order to establish and lead a transitional government," stressed José Jéri, who will lead the country until 26 July 2026 with the heavy task of organising general elections next April.

As for Dina Boluarte, the Peruvian public prosecutor's office has asked the courts to bar her from leaving the country for 18 to 36 months, in order to finalise the investigations against her for "offences of money laundering to the detriment of the State" and "corruption and abuse of power".

According to the public prosecutor's office, "this measure aims to guarantee Boluarte's presence during the course of the criminal proceedings and [to guard against] a possible flight from the national territory". Before being stripped of the presidential office, the former president had been shaken by several scandals concerning her acquisition of watches and jewellery and for having allowed herself "a rhinoplasty carried out in secret in 2023 in violation of the law".

A South American country, Peru has for some years been going through "the worst period of political instability in its modern history, with seven presidents in nearly nine years".

By Chiaka Doumbia

a6868.t:
(ክፍል ሁለት)
በደምስ ጫንያለው (ዶ/ር)
ኢምፔሪያል ካፒታሊስቶችን መፍጠር የንጉሡና የደርግ ዘመን
አሜሪካ ከመፈጠሯ በፊት ጀምሮም ሆነ ከዚያም በኋላ ካፒታሊስትና ኢምፔሪያሊስት ኢትዮጵያውያንን በኢትዮጵያ ምድር ላይ መፍጠር ይቻል ነበር፡፡ የነበረንን ሙግት ለጊዜው ገታናድርገውና ዛሬም አገራዊ ፖስፕኢ ቀርፆ የሚተገብር ቁርጠኝ ዜጋ፣ መንግሥትና የአመራር ተቋማት ካገኘች ኢትዮጵያ ዜጋና ትውልደ ኢትዮጵያውያን የሆኑ ኢምፔሪያል ካፒታሊስቶች ሊኖሯት ይቻላል፡፡
በእርግጥ ቀደም ሲልም ይህንን የተረዱት መሪዎቿ፣ በተለይ አፄ ኃይለ ሥላሴና መንግሥታቸው ኢትዮጵያውያን ካፒታሊስቶችንና ኢምፔሪያሊስቶችን የመፍጠር፣ የማሳደግ፣ የማጎልበትና የማብዛት ፖሊሲ አቅጣጫ ይዘው ተንቀሳቅሰው ነበር፡፡ ለምሳሌ የ1945 ዓ.ም. ‹‹መሬት ለጭሰኛው›› አዋጅ ጭሰኛውን የመሬት ባለቤት በማድረግ፣ ከትንንሽ ማሳ ወደ መካከለኛ ስፋት ማሳ ይዞታ ያላቸውን አራሾች ለመፍጠር ታቅዶ ነበር፡፡ በተጓዳኝም በግብርናው መስክ ኢትዮጵያዊ ካፒታሊስቶችን መፍጠር ጭምር፡፡
አፄ ኃይለ ሥላሴ ጭሰኛው ባለ ጋሻ መሬት፣ የግል አራሽ ብሎም የሀብት ፈጣሪ፣ በኢንዱስትሪው ዘርፍም፣ በተለይ በግብርና አግሮ ፕሮሰሲንግ፣ ኢትዮጵያውያን ባለሀብቶች፣ ኢንቨስተር ካፒታሊስቶች እየተፈጠሩና እየጎለበቱ እንዲመጡ ለማድረግ ከ1940 ዓ.ም. አጋማሽ ጀምረው አገራዊ ፖስፕኢ በመቅረፅና በመተግበር፣ እንደ አግባቡብም መሬትን ለጭሰኛው ለማከፋፈል አዋጅ በማውጣትና የመሳሰሉትን የሕግ ማዕቀፎች በመዘርጋት እንቅስቃሴ ማድረግ ቢጀምሩም፣ ይህ የፖሊሲ አቅጣጫቸው ግን በውጭ ኢምፔሪያሊስት አገሮች ተንኮልና አሻጥር ተገታባቸው፡፡ ከፋይናንስ አንፃር ከመደበኛው ባንክ በተጨማሪ የዛሬውን ልማት ባንክ ዓይነት የፖሊሲ ባንክ ለዚሁ ጉዳይ ያግዝ ዘንድ አቋቁመዋል፡፡ የግብዓት አቅራቢ ለምሳሌ ማዳበሪያን የሚያቀርቡ የንግድ ተቋማትን መሥርተውም ነበር፡፡
አፄው ከመሬት ጋር የተቆራኘውን የመሠረተ ልማት ሥራ ለመሥራት የአገር ውስጥ የፋይናንስ ተቋማትና አቅም አነስተኛ በመሆኑ ሰፊ የልማት ፕሮጀክት በአገራዊ ሙያተኞች መሪነት አዘጋጅተው ብድር ለማግኘት ያልጠየቁት ያደጉ ምዕራብ አገሮች መሪዎችና ተቋማት አልነበሩም፡፡ ምዕራባውያኑ ግን ፈቃደኛ አልሆኑም፡፡ እነሱ ብድር አንሰጥም ማለታቸውን ሲያውቁ ፊታቸውን ወደ ሩሲያ በማዞር፣ በወቅቱ በጣም ከፍተኛ የሆነ 400 ሚሊዮን ሩብል ብድር ከሩሲያ መንግሥት አግኝተው ነበር፡፡ በዚህም ከመሬት ጋር የተቆራኘውን ፕሮጀክት ለመተግበር ጄኔራል ሙሉጌታ ቡሊ የሚመሩት አስፈጻሚ አካል ተቋቁሞ እንቅስቃሴ ተጀምሮ ነበር፡፡ ይህንን የተረዱት ነጮች በተለይ አሜሪካ መራሽ የምዕራቡ አገሮች፣ በተንኮልና በሴራ ዕሳቤያቸው ፀንተው ፕሮጀክቱን ለማሰናከል ቆርጠው ተነሱ፡፡ እነዚህ የውጭ ኃይሎች ይህንን ፕሮጀክትም አትተገብሩትም ሲሉ ማስፈራራት የጀመሩት ገና ጃንሆይ ሩሲያ ሆነው ብድሩን ሲፈራረሙ ነበር፡፡ የዚህን ጉዳይ ሙሉ ታሪክና በአጠቃላይም በንጉሡ ጊዜ ተጀምረው ስለነበሩ አገራዊ ኢምፔሪያሊስቶችን የመፍጠር እንቅስቃሴና ለዚያ የሚውል የመሠረተ ልማት ግንባታ እስከ ዛሬው ህዳሴ ግድብ ፕሮጀክት ቀረፃ ጭምር፣ ደጃዝማች ወልደ ሰማዕት ገብረ ወልድ በ2012 ዓ.ም. ‹‹ሕይወቴ ለአገሬ ኢትዮጵያና ለወገኖቼ ኢትዮጵያውያን የነበረኝ የሥራ ጥማት›› በሚል ባሳተሙት መጽሐፍ ከምዕራፍ 8 እስከ 11 በስፋትና በጥልቀት ተጽፎ ይገኛል፡፡

የግብዓቶች ነፃ እንቅስቃሴና የመደራጀት ፖስፕኢ፣ የአገሪቱ ዜጎች ከአነስተኛ የግብርና የእርሻን ጨምሮ፣ የኢንዱስትሪና አገልግሎት ዘርፍ ሥራዎችና ተቋማት ግንባታ፣ በሁሉም ዘርፍ ወደ መካከለኛና ከፍተኛ ኢንዱስትሪያል ሥራዎችና አደረጃጀቶች ይሸጋገሩ ዘንድ ግብዓቶች (ሰው ኃይልና ካፒታልን ጨምሮ) በነፃ የኢኮኖሚ ምኅዳር ውስጥ መንቀሳቀስ አለባቸው፡፡ ዜጎች በነፃነት በየትኛውም የአገሪቱ ክፍል ተዛውረው ሥራ የመፍጠር፣ ሀብትና ንብረት የማፍራት፣ ባሉበት አካባቢም ሆነ በሌሌሎች አካባቢዎች ኢንቨስት የማድረግ ሕጋዊ ድጋፍና ጥበቃ እንዲኖራቸው ይገባል፡፡ አምራቾችም በየትኛውም ዘርፍና የምርት ዓይነት የመደራጀት፣ ማኅበራት የማቋቋም፣ የገበሬዎች ማኅበርን ጨምሮ፣ እንዲሁም በግልም ሆነ በማኅበሮቻቸው አማካይነት በግብዓት አቅርቦትና ተደራሽነት ሆነ በሸቀጥ ገበያ የሎጂስቲክ ሆነ የዋጋ ተጠቃሚነት ይኖራቸው ዘንድ ፖስፕኢዎቹ ግልጽና በሕግ የተቋጩ መሆን አለባቸው፡፡

እኔ ከአሜሪካኖች የኢኮኖሚ ታሪክ የቀሰምኩት አስተምህሮ አንዱ ፖለቲካውን በዕሳቤ፣ ቁስና ፋይናንስ አቅማቸው በጎለበቱ ኢንተርፕረነር ፖለቲከኞች እንዲመራ የማድረግ መርሀቸው ነው፡፡ ፖለቲከኞቹ በዕሳቤም ሆነ በቁስና ፋይናንስ ሀብታም የሆኑ ናቸው፡፡ እነዚህ መሰል ፖለቲከኞችና የሕዝብ አስተዳዳሪዎች በቅድሚያ ለአሜሪካ ፍላጎትና ጥቅም ይቆማሉ እንጂ፣ ‹‹ዴሞክራሲን በመገንባትና በማስረፅ›› የደሃ አገር ፖለቲከኞችን ዓይነት የፖለቲካ ሸቀጥ ፍብረካና ንግድ ላይ ጉልበት፣ ዕውቀትና ጊዜያቸውን አያጠፉም፡፡ ታሪካቸውም ይህንን አያሳየንም፡፡ ዛሬም ቢሆን አሜሪካኖች በየትኛውም የዓለም ክፍል የጦር ሠራዊታቸውን የሚያሠማሩት ዴሞክራሲን ለማሥፈን ሳይሆን የጥሬ ዕቃ ምንጭ የሆኑ አካባቢዎችን ለመያዝ፣ የተመረቱ ሸቀጦችን ለማራገፍ፣ በአጠቃላይ ለግብዓቶችም ሆነ ለምርት ውጤቶች ገበያ ለማግኘትና ሰፊ ይዞታ ይኖራቸው ዘንድ ያላቸውን ፍላጎትና ተጠቃሚነት ለማስከበር ነው፡፡
ለኢትዮጵያ እውነተኛ አገር ወዳድና አልሚ ባለሀብቶች፣ ካፒታሊስቶችና ኢምፔሪያሊስቶች ይኖሯት ዘንድ የሚያስፈልጓት በድህነት ዕሳቤ ያደጉ ፖለቲከኞችና የሕዝብ አስተዳዳሪዎች ሳይሆኑ፣ በግል ጥረታቸውና ሥራቸው፣ በኢኮኖሚ ገቢያቸው፣ በንብረትና ሀብት ክምችታቸው ከዚህም ላይ ተመርኩዘው በአካባቢያቸውና በአገር ደረጃ ሥራ ፈጣሪነታቸውና ሁለንተናዊ ተፅዕኖ ፈጣሪነታቸው አንቱታን ያተረፉ፣ በዕውቀትና ሀብት ፈጣሪነት የተካኑ፣ የኢንተርፕረነርነት ልምዱና ተሞክሮው ያላቸው፣ የፖለቲካ ሰዎችና የመንግሥት ባለሥልጣናት ናቸው፡፡
በድህነት ዕሳቤ ያላደጉ ሲባል አንድ ዜጋ ከትንሽ ጥሪት ወይም የኢንተርፕረነር ዕሳቤ ተነስቶ ሀብት ማፍራት አይችልም ማለት አይደለም፡፡ ይችላል፣ ትችላለች፡፡ በሌላ አገላለጽ በገቢው፣ በንብረት ይዞታውና ኑሮው ደሃ የተባለ ዜጋ ሀብታም፣ ሀብታም የነበረ ደግሞ ደሃ ሊሆን ይችላል፡፡ ልዩነቱ ጠንክሮ መሥራት፣ ተጣጥሮ ያለውን/ያላትን ዕውቀት፣ ጥሪት፣ ሰዋዊ ካፒታል፣ መሬትና ተጓዳኝ ንብረቶች በማቆራኘት ወደ ተሻለ ገቢ አመንጪ፣ ሥራ ፈጣሪ፣ ቆጣቢና ከፋይናንስ ተቋማት ጋር ተሳስሮ ወደ ኢንቨስትመንት ሥራ ውስጥ መግባት፣ በሒደትም የሚያጋጥሙ ችግሮችንና ተግዳሮቶችን ተቋቁሞ፣ በዘላቂ የሀብት ማፍራት እንቅስቃሴ ውጤታማ ሆኖ መገኘት ላይ ነው፡፡ ይህ እንዲሆን ደግሞ ኢኮኖሚው ከድህነት ዕሳቤ በተላቀቁ ዜጎችና ፖለቲከኞች መመራት መቻል አለበት፡፡ ዜጋውም እነዚህን መሰል ፖለቲከኞችና የሕዝብ አስተዳዳሪዎች የመፍጠሪያና የማብቂያ ሥርዓትን ለመዘርጋትና ለመገንባት ተገቢ አገራዊና የሚተገበር የፖስፕኢ ቀርፃና አደረጃጀት ላይ ትኩረት ሰጥቶ መወያየት፣ መምከርና በተስማማባቸው ላይ ወደ መተገበሩ መትመም አለበት፡፡
ከአዘጋጁ፡- ጸሐፊው የግብርና ኢኮኖሚ ተመራማሪና ባለሙያ ሲሆኑ፣ ጽሑፉ የእሳቸውን አመለካከት ብቻ የሚያንፀባርቅ መሆኑን እየገለጽን፣ በኢሜይል አድራሻቸው [email protected] ማግኘት ይቻላል፡፡

(Part Two)
By Demis Chanyalew (PhD)

Creating imperial capitalists: the era of the Emperor and the Derg

Both before America came into being and afterwards, it was possible to create capitalist and imperialist Ethiopians on Ethiopian soil. Let us set aside for the moment the argument we have been having: even today, if Ethiopia finds committed citizens, a government and leadership institutions that formulate and implement a national POSPEI (policy, strategy, programme and implementation), she can have imperial capitalists who are Ethiopian citizens and people of Ethiopian descent.

Indeed, her leaders understood this earlier; in particular Emperor Haile Selassie and his government moved with a policy direction of creating, growing, strengthening and multiplying Ethiopian capitalists and imperialists. For example, the 1945 E.C. "Land to the Tenant" proclamation was planned to make the tenant a landowner and to create cultivators moving from small plots to medium-sized holdings - and, alongside that, to create Ethiopian capitalists in the agricultural field.

Emperor Haile Selassie, from the middle of the 1940s E.C. onward, began to move - by formulating and implementing a national POSPEI, by issuing a proclamation to distribute land to the tenant as appropriate, and by laying down similar legal frameworks - so that the tenant would become a holder of a gasha of land, a private cultivator and then a wealth creator, and so that in the industrial sector too, particularly in agro-processing, Ethiopian investors and investor-capitalists would be created and strengthened. But this policy direction of his was blocked by the intrigue and sabotage of foreign imperialist countries. On the financial side, in addition to the ordinary bank, he established a policy bank of the kind of today's Development Bank to assist this purpose. He had also founded commercial enterprises that supplied inputs, for example fertiliser.

Because domestic financial institutions and capacity were small for carrying out the land-related infrastructure work, there was hardly a leader or institution of the developed Western countries from whom the Emperor did not request loans, having prepared broad development projects under the leadership of national professionals. The Westerners, however, were unwilling. When he learned that they were refusing to lend, he turned his face to Russia and obtained from the Russian government a loan of 400 million roubles, a very large sum at the time. With this, an executive body led by General Mulugeta Buli was established to implement the land-related project and work was begun. Understanding this, the whites - particularly the American-led Western countries - held firm to their scheming and conspiratorial mindset and resolved to derail the project. These foreign forces began threatening that the project would not be implemented even while His Majesty was in Russia signing the loan. The full history of this matter, and in general of the movement begun in the Emperor's time to create national imperialists and the infrastructure construction serving it - up to and including the design of today's Renaissance Dam project - is written extensively and deeply in chapters 8 to 11 of the book Dejazmach Wolde Semayat Gebre Wold published in 2012 E.C. under the title "My Life: The Thirst for Work I Had for My Country Ethiopia and for My Fellow Ethiopians."

As I understood from the Dejazmach's book, the whites, the Western colonisers, having observed the movement to organise Ethiopians' economic growth and development - particularly the natural resources on and within the land - under Ethiopian leadership and through large and modern institutions, resolved once again to weaken the country, thinking that a country that had defeated whites with traditional weapons and organisation, if it prospered economically, created its own national imperial capitalists and on that basis became a prosperous people and country, would challenge them in various fields around the world. They had already carried out the Western colonising movement in Menelik's time through Italian execution. In particular, they made great efforts, using the Somali government, to weaken and break up the country through the eastern part of our country. In other parts of the country too they began to conspire and carry out evil deeds to divide and disintegrate Ethiopia by race, ethnicity, language and religion in every way they could. Recently, Atnafu and Mesfin (PhD), drawing on the book published in English in 1935 by Roman Prochazka under the title "Abyssinia, the Powder Barrel," presented an analysis of the contemporary content of this machination of theirs after the defeat of Italy, in an English article in The Habesha magazine in December 2021 (2014 E.C.) titled "Prochazka's Death Throes at the State Department, Ethiopia and the USA." In their article they made clear to us how hard the American-led developed Western governments work to break up Ethiopia, and how they have planned and are implementing ethnicity- and religion-targeted weakening and, where possible, destruction, in order to secure not only their interests inside Ethiopia but their desires and interests in Africa and in the lands of black people. I recommend on this occasion that you read their full article.

As stated above, the white colonisers of Europe and North America, having realised that the Ethiopians' 1945 E.C. land-to-the-tenant proclamation, and particularly the large development project movement led by General Mulugeta, would hasten their fate of being pushed out of African countries and would strengthen the Pan-African movement, plotted and began to move conspiratorially, concluding that they must stop Ethiopia's all-round movement through various acts of sabotage and destruction. The 1953 E.C. attempted coup and the killing of well-known people such as General Mulugeta Buli were one part of this conspiracy. Thereafter they intensified and continued dividing the citizens Ethiopia sent abroad for higher education from 1940 E.C. onward into camps of various political factions and ideological advocacies, and by race, clan, ethnicity, language, colour and religion - destabilising the economic and public-administration system in the name of establishing democracy, and creating sabotage and confusion within the structure of government and in the security and intelligence institutions. Recruiting many educated elites into modern economic and political collaboration, they deployed them for evil work through various international multilateral and bilateral institutions. They also caused the educated elite to begin killing one another in political wrangling. In this respect, Marx and Engels and their like did not fail to deceive us.

Those who fell victim to the ideological games created by the philosophers and politicians of these Western imperial capitalist countries were not the educated elites within the Western or Eastern imperialist countries, nor the capitalists and imperialists engaged in the economic and commercial sectors, but the educated patriotic elites, the wealthy, and the capitalists who had been emerging in developing countries like ours. In Ethiopia, the Ethiopian investors and capitalists who had been growing stronger in Emperor Haile Selassie's time - particularly those transitioning from small- to medium-scale industry in farming and agricultural manufacturing - were made to be destroyed or stunted in the name of revolution, through the revolutionary movement and killing campaigns of extremist politicians sent from America and Europe, of the kinds referred to in our country as "White Terror" and "Red Terror."

Those who worked behind the scenes so that the Derg, in the name of socialism, would destroy the wealthy and the emerging national imperial capitalists were mostly not elites educated in socialist Russia or China, but forces educated in North America and Europe and organised in various political parties. Since it is difficult to obtain documentary evidence of the conspiracies of developed countries' intelligence institutions, many suspect that most of those parties received substantial financial, training, technical and technological support from those institutions. Through the conspiracy of these institutions and through their executing collaborators, modern farms, industries, and domestic and export trading enterprises started by Ethiopian investors in various parts of the country were nationalised and destroyed.

The positive investment movement of the Emperor's era - in which citizens moved from one province and locality of the country to another and rose from small economic activity to medium and higher levels - and the transition to creating manufacturing and trading enterprises were made to fail. The vision and practice of citizens who were transitioning from small agricultural, industrial and service-sector enterprises to medium and large economic organisations in various parts of the country were made to be stunted.

For example, in Wolaita province, the broad modern farm developments of investors created and growing under the leadership of Dejazmach Wolde Semayat were disrupted. On the private side, for instance, a man named Ato Tsegaye Gashe of the Bekoji area - the owner of today's Becas Chemicals Company and the father of Bekele Tsegaye - travelled far from the area where he was born, from Chacha in Shewa province, and operated as a successful entrepreneur in trade in the Lemu and Bilbilo district of Arsi; in farming too, starting from owning no land at all, he came to own up to fifty hectares of land by purchase and bought a tractor, and just as he was about to start modern farming the revolution derailed him - as documented in the book "The Road to Success," written by Bekele himself and published in 2015 E.C. That this revolution, tuned to socialist ideology, derailed the growth and multiplication of many national investors is not something to be told with one example alone; as I tried to explain above, it is an example and a further reminder that it was a historical loss inflicted by conspiracies woven by foreign forces and by the plots of educated Ethiopian elites caught in their intrigue. Nor did it remain merely a historical loss thereafter. To this day the execution of this conspiracy continues through economic and political collaborators bought by foreign forces.

Let me emphasise one thing here. Through the instrumentality of Ethiopian economic and political collaborators (dual collaborators), foreign forces have implemented their conspiracy of stunting and destroying Ethiopian national investors and capitalists, and they continue to do so today. I have made this understanding and conclusion of mine known repeatedly not only in this article but also in the books and newspaper columns I have written recently. Yet, to this day - though it is hard to say how many we number - when I and other Ethiopians state that Ethiopia's multi-context, all-round development and growth is still being hijacked and stunted by the conspiracy, intrigue and sabotage of foreign forces, our advice and our arguments are seen to be given a political reading.

The ideas, advice and reminders we give are twisted into being treated as notices and cautions intended to buy time for political actors; to appease and cajole social groups in various parts of our country for the sake of politicians' games; to externalise the causes of the problems and challenges they face in economic and social contexts; to keep politicians from focusing on consulting and discussing on the basis of experiences grounded in internal national values; and, on that basis, to keep them from being reprimanded and isolated. But my reminders and cautions, and those of people like me, are not tied to such political calculations.

Because in Ethiopia - not only today but for many generations, especially over the past four hundred years - there have been and continue to be country-destroying conspiracies and evil missions carried out by foreign forces, and because these are documented in historical records, it is on the basis of studying and examining these that we present our reminders and cautions.

One of the matters we Ethiopians need to know and understand deeply is that the work being desired, planned and carried out today, under the leadership, conspiracy and support of foreign forces, for our country to break apart, was founded before the country today called the USA came into being. Before that country was created, European powers such as Portugal, England, Germany and Italy challenged Ethiopia's sovereignty and national unity in many directions and by many methods. After America's creation this has continued in strengthened form. If we do not study, examine and grasp this matter with appropriate depth and breadth, it will be very difficult for us Ethiopians to find a solution, in unity and with our social diversity preserved, to the existential problem we face today. Here, by way of example, I will survey a few of the documented efforts of foreign forces to break up Ethiopia and then move to the next part of my article.

Alemayehu Abebe translated the book written by Andrzej Bartnicki and Joanna Mantel-Niecko on Ethiopian history and published it for our reading in 2006 E.C. under the title "History of Ethiopia, from the Beginning to the Present Era." The disintegration of the state that threatened Ethiopia in the 16th century through foreign forces, particularly the Portuguese Jesuits, on religious pretexts, as well as the thirty years of continuous civil conflict and war, are documented in this book. Emperor Fasil, who understood these forces' evil mission and country-destroying activity, ordered at the time that foreign nationals be swept out of the country. It is documented on page 337 of the book that in Menelik's time the Italian Baratieri sincerely believed he would "divide Ethiopia." That Europeans, particularly Britain, France and Italy, plotted at the beginning of 1890 E.C. to carve up Ethiopia is explained on page 406. That these forces did subversive work focused on organising war from outside and on a coup strategy from inside is written on page 447, including a description of the coup in which Negadras Gebre Hiwot Baykedagn and others participated. That the Italians divided Ethiopia into six governorates, split it by religion and clan, prepared a settlement territory in order to exploit the economy, to rule the people by oppression, and to bring their own citizens from Italy and settle them, is written in the book from pages 535 to 557. The book has also shared with us the information that when Ethiopians made the Italians leave the country in 1941, they blew up with mines the roads and bridges that had been built.

Creating imperial capitalists, from the EPRDF to today's government

Over the past four decades, too, neither the EPRDF government nor today's Prosperity government has been seen to reverse the historical loss we suffered through the sabotage and intrigue of foreign forces in the Emperor's and the Derg's time, or to formulate a POSPEI so that Ethiopia would create capitalist imperialists of her own. Not only did they fail to focus on establishing an economic system that creates, grows, strengthens and multiplies national imperial capitalists - worse, as in the socialist Derg era, the country appears to be being driven into a system entangled in a command-economy and developmental-state mindset, with the implication that the private economic sector should be stunted and that the economic activity from farming and other agro-industrial activities to the manufacturing and service industry must be held by federal and regional government institutions and led by the organisations and structures we ourselves establish. In addition, it appears that the door has been opened for the economy to become a victim of the corporatocracy - that is, the system created by the developed countries' international multilateral financial and trade organisations such as the World Bank and the IMF, and by cross-border companies - and that they are romping in it.

The exemplary significance of the experience of Ato Tsegaye Gashe, which I described earlier, is great in showing that small farmers in agriculture and entrepreneurial Ethiopians in other sectors can start from zero material assets and become owners of modern, commercially oriented farms. In this regard, although there were good beginnings in the Emperor's era, they were derailed under the Derg's socialist leadership. Afterwards, under both the EPRDF and the Prosperity government, it has not been possible to create national imperial capitalists, because no POSPEI has been formulated and implemented that would allow even some of the many small-holding farmers and pastoralists we have seen on television screens being awarded for years and repeatedly described as having become millionaires to transition into capitalist, modern and commercially oriented cultivators. One reason for this is the poverty mindset and weakness of our own national leaders and government institutions; another is the foreign forces' frustrating or distorting of the government's policy direction in the name of various dollar-laden projects. In this regard, the example I present is the matter of cluster farming.

I tried to make Ethiopians aware of the dangerous conspiracy of foreign forces carried out through the Agricultural Transformation Institute under the name of the Producer Farmers' Cluster Project, which crushes small and entrepreneurial farmers and stunts their growth, in a two-part article published in the Reporter newspaper on 2 and 9 Tahsas 2015 E.C. under the title "The Narrative that Opposes Cluster Farming." In that article I presented an explanation that cluster farming is not new in Ethiopia, that it existed from the Emperor's time and, in the EPRDF period too, from around 2000 E.C. was tuned to a demand-led conception, whereas today, as I say, it has taken a distorted supply-led course. Earlier, too, I gave relatively extensive explanations of the POSPEI content and results of short- and long-term cluster agricultural work in my books of 2009, 2012 and 2013 E.C. In brief, however, I have found it appropriate to cite certain matters again here, and have presented them as follows.

In the newspaper article indicated above I presented my professional position that the cluster farming movement and project supported by foreign forces' dollars has become an obstacle preventing the Ethiopian farmer from establishing, on his own initiative, modern and commercially oriented farms and other agricultural enterprises on land ranging from small plots to large holdings counted in tens of thousands of hectares, and thereby preventing national imperial capitalists in the sector from being born, growing and multiplying. This does not mean, however - as I also explained - that the recent cluster farming movement was unnecessary or ineffective when viewed from the standpoint of short- and long-term policy formulation and implementation.

Cluster farming may be an option for increasing the productivity and output of selected crops and of animals and animal products in the short term. This has been confirmed by the positive change recently obtained by the Prosperity-led government in wheat and other crops, as well as in animal products. But for bringing structural change in the agricultural economic sector over the long term and realising industrial agriculture under citizens' leadership, the cluster farming approach is an obstructive and indeed fatal strategy.

In the manufacturing industry and service sector, it has been arranged since the Derg era that Ethiopian national imperial capitalists should not exist. Although the sector appears to have been given attention by the Prosperity government, gaps still remain in POSPEI formulation and implementation. Even today, under a policy direction based on sniffing out dollars, and a distorted strategy tuned to attracting investors and to technology transfer, there is no POSPEI direction set to create, grow, strengthen and multiply national imperial capitalists in these sectors - only proceeding with a few investors who do not stand on their own feet. That cluster organisation is the main direction of focus in this sector is stated in Part Three of the Prosperity government's 2013 to 2022 E.C. development plan document. However, the change registered is minimal relative to what is expected. For example, in edible oil production, not even meaningful action has been taken so that our factories that were started in the Emperor's era and had reached small to medium production scale would recover and be strengthened. I tried to inform Ethiopians, in an article I published in the Reporter newspaper of 7 Hidar 2015 E.C., that these factories have been weakened and many of them closed since the EPRDF period.

In general, the agricultural and industrial development POSPEI formulation and implementation carried out from the EPRDF period to today is largely a POSPEI direction set on political narrative, on short-term problem-solving and on serving as an accompaniment to political work, rather than on an approach tuned to lasting, competitive national economic growth and development. This must be corrected and must enter the necessary development direction.

Here I want readers to grasp one thing again. That is, the criticism I presented above does not proceed from the conclusion that there are no farming or other agricultural, industrial or service-sector development works carried out and results registered in the EPRDF's or the present Prosperity government's time. I was a professional adviser behind some of those works. In many of my articles I have also made known our role in urging the necessity of the recent expansion of wheat and irrigated agriculture, as well as the positive results obtained.

Particularly over the past five years, many effective works have been done through the commitment and unrelenting follow-up of the senior leadership of the Prosperity Party government. In my estimation, however, the works are very small relative to Ethiopia's present capacity and competence. There are many gaps and distortions in placing the Ethiopian economy on a foundation led by Ethiopians, with foreign forces as helpers and partners. Much, much more must be done to bring structural change in Ethiopia, particularly in agriculture, and in general to make the economy internationally competitive in every sector and led by national imperial capitalists. We must do effective work with the capacity and ability we have, while planning and building the capacity we lack. In that regard, I hold the position that today the process of formulating and implementing an appropriate national POSPEI that goes beyond political discourse is thin and is not aligned with a practice of protecting the interests and benefits of the country and the people. Reflecting on the matter and returning to the appropriate direction must not be something that is given time.

The necessity of a strong army and defence institution for a strong economy

Earlier I tried to indicate in bird's-eye fashion, weaving in the historical background, the role played by the army and the defence, security and intelligence institutions of the colony and later of the United States of America in creating her national imperial capitalists. That army and those institutions are making America a leading competitor in the world in her economic content and imperialist forces today as well.

Today too, around our world, the role of military institutions and their organisation is great for Americans to obtain the raw materials they want, especially mineral sites, and markets for selling and offloading goods - particularly to grip developing countries tightly, directly or indirectly. The African country the Democratic Republic of Congo, because of its uranium deposits, and the countries of Central Asia and of North and West Africa, because of their oil deposits, are under the tight control of these forces.

For other economically developed and prosperous countries of North America, Europe and Asia too, the role of their armies and associated defence and security institutions has been great in reaching the level they have reached.

That China today has come to challenge America in her all-round content is because she built her national imperialist capitalists linked to strong army, defence, security and intelligence institutions. In the Western conception she is a socialist country that has no democratic system and is not led by a free economic system. This is merely fuel for print and electronic media narrative and discourse; it has not become something that stops China from taking economic supremacy in our world. There is one main thing we must learn from this Chinese experience: that whatever ideology countries follow, what must first be given focus and worked on in order to be competitive in the world market and to obtain raw materials and natural resources to exploit, as well as markets for selling goods and services, is creating, growing, strengthening and multiplying national imperial capitalists.

Therefore, in order for Ethiopia truly to have economic and social development sufficient for the prosperity of her people and her country, she must build her own national imperial capitalists and an invincible army and defence, security and intelligence institutions, and must be able to lead these with lasting capacity and competence.

There is one matter I wish to emphasise here. That is, I am not saying that the formulation and implementation of a POSPEI for building a strong army and defence, security and intelligence institutions should precede that of a strong economic and social development POSPEI. It is proper, however, to understand that both works are necessary to each other's strength and effectiveness, and that they should be led in an integrated and expedited way. It was starting from these substantive ideas that, before the Prosperity Party and its ideas were known or spoken of, in a review study paper I wrote in 2000 E.C. in the EPRDF era and presented at a professional forum meeting, I began to argue that Ethiopia's POSPEI formulation must change from poverty-focused to pragmatic prosperity-focused. The English edition of this paper is published in the post-conference book of the tenth annual conference of the Ethiopian Agricultural Economics Professional Association, printed in 2000 E.C. (2008 in the Gregorian calendar). I recommend that you read it.

Conclusion and recommended POSPEI directions

This article has indicated that, in order for the Ethiopian economy to change from the weak position, poverty and poverty-dominated content it is in today to a better level - and for that change to be expressed in improvement in the income and living standards of the majority of citizens, and for them to become users of technology fit for the times in all contexts - a POSPEI framework must be formulated and implemented with focus on three themes.

The first makes us aware that the strong economy that can exist in Ethiopia is one not based on race and ethnicity; the second indicates that the POSPEI framework of Ethiopia's economic development must be one of creating, growing, strengthening and multiplying national imperial capitalists. The third POSPEI framework, which must be formulated and implemented in linkage with the preceding themes, is tied to organising a strong army and building defence, security and intelligence institutions.

In formulating and implementing POSPEI frameworks on matters around these three themes, it is possible to incorporate positive lessons we learn from other countries. For example, the POSPEI direction we learn from the Americans is that a growing and prospering economy requires issuing and implementing the proper and necessary principles and laws so that citizens may, freely and on their private initiative, with the knowledge, labour and assets they have, move from place to place and from country to country inside and outside their country and carry out economic activity; and thereby earn income, own property including land, and, with associated activity of developing, selling and exchanging, create wealth, invest, and rise from a lower level of capitalist status to a high level of imperial capitalist status.

What we do not learn from them is the kind of thing they did from the 16th to the 19th century: using military force to make land and the natural resources and bounty on and within it serve the economic supremacy of one race, tribe or section of society, and the associated formulation and implementation of a POSPEI of genocide and persecution.

Although there are many POSPEI formulation, revision and amendment matters that revolve around these three themes separately or in their linkage and integration, further below I have presented recommendations indicating the future direction for Ethiopia's coming time on five selected POSPEI matters that I say must be given priority. The five POSPEI directions revolve around land, the natural resources it holds within it, various fiscal, macroeconomic and trade POSPEI matters, the free and private economic activity of inputs (including people), and the formulation and implementation of a public administration and political-trade POSPEI befitting this.

Land POSPEI: in order for there to be genuine investors, capitalists and imperial capitalists in Ethiopia, land policy must change from its present government-focused content to a private-ownership-focused policy and development strategy. A private-ownership-focused policy does not exclude land being under communal/joint, community and government ownership. When it is said that it should be private-ownership-focused, however, land ownership must in no way be given to foreign nationals until the country has grown and has the institutions that enable it to administer, control and protect its land and associated natural resources as the countries said to be developed and prosperous do.

Note

In presenting this policy direction, I have also understood, to the level I understood it, the amended Rural Land Administration and Use Proclamation No. 456/1997 approved in the House of Peoples' Representatives on 6 Ginbot 2016 E.C. I myself, together with professional colleagues, read and reviewed this proclamation and other associated proclamations and presented a broad recommendation for the revision and amendment of land POSPEI and development revolving around 32 major issues in my book written in 2012 E.C. under the title "The Economy, the Three Politicians and Policy"; I therefore recommend that readers read this book of mine so that they may gain additional understanding of the timely recommendation I presented above.

Natural resource and bounty development POSPEI: the POSPEI for extracting, developing and using the water, the various minerals, petroleum, forests and forest products, etc., on and within the land must be formulated and implemented in a private-citizen-led manner. Being citizen-led, however, it is also possible, as appropriate, to follow a development direction that involves foreign nationals - through a development strategy jointly by citizens with the government and with investors coming from foreign countries, with shares of finance and technology use, or in a structure organised as a share company or corporation.
